purpose: Asset-independent English semantic-role gold for blind judging of renderable URDF link names in the frozen Table 2 Naming matched panel.

construction_inputs: the frozen matched-panel protocol named in parent_protocol
public official manufacturer product, support, and owner-documentation pages listed in sources
independence.statement: Roles and synonyms were fixed from category definitions and public product terminology, without observing evaluated names or artifacts.

scope.unit_of_judgment: one renderable link name interpreted together with the link's visible geometry, placement, and motion
out_of_scope: internal components not represented as distinct renderable links
materials, colors, style, and brand names
kinematic correctness beyond what is needed to identify a visible semantic role

normalization.comparison: case-insensitive after splitting camel case and treating spaces, hyphens, and underscores as token separators
allowed_morphology: left, right, upper, lower, top, bottom, front, rear, inner, and outer qualifiers when geometrically correct
normalization.compound_rule: A listed synonym may occur inside a more specific, truthful compound, but substring coincidence inside an unrelated token is not acceptance.
normalization.generic_token_rule: A generic token alone, or with only an opaque number or hash, is not a semantic role name.
normalization.truthfulness_rule: A lexical match is rejected when geometry, location, or motion clearly realizes a different role.

judging_contract.role_assignment: Assign each named renderable link to the most specific supported canonical role, an allowed specialization, other_truthful_semantic, generic_placeholder, or incorrect_semantic.
judging_contract.minimal_role_interpretation: Minimal required roles describe category-level functional coverage. They do not require one link per role: fused geometry may realize multiple roles, and absent separate segmentation is not a naming error.
judging_contract.optional_role_interpretation: An optional role is judged only when that component is visibly realized as a distinct renderable link. Its absence is never an error.
judging_contract.unlisted_truthful_names: A precise, truthful component name not listed as a synonym is labeled other_truthful_semantic rather than incorrect; judges must record it for adjudication without changing this frozen gold.
judging_contract.synonym_boundary: Synonyms license the semantic role, not arbitrary token replacement across distinct roles such as door versus door frame or rack versus rack rail.
judging_contract.multi_role_links: For a fused link, accept the most inclusive truthful name. Do not require the name to enumerate every fused subrole.
judging_contract.metric_gate: This gold alone does not activate semantic metrics. The parent protocol's requirement for three blind judges remains mandatory.

global_instance_discriminability.singleton_rule: Do not require an instance qualifier for a role represented exactly once.
global_instance_discriminability.repeated_role_rule: Every simultaneously visible repeated instance of the same role must be distinguishable as a set by stable semantic qualifiers or deterministic ordinals.
qualifier_priority: functional identity, such as hot versus cold
compartment or level, such as freezer versus refrigerator or upper versus lower
laterality or depth, such as left versus right or front versus rear
one-based ordinal in a documented stable order
global_instance_discriminability.ordinal_rule: Ordinals are acceptable only when no more informative visible distinction exists and the ordering convention is stated consistently for the asset.
global_instance_discriminability.opaque_id_rule: Random hashes, source IDs, and non-consecutive opaque numbers do not establish instance discriminability.
global_instance_discriminability.group_rule: A single link that visibly represents a coherent inseparable group may use a plural or group name and is not penalized for lacking per-member indices.

microwave.category_definition: microwave cooking appliance; microwave oven is an accepted category synonym

minimal_required_roles.definition: the main enclosure and structural body around the cooking chamber
the closure providing access to the microwave cooking chamber

optional_roles.presence_condition: only when a distinct graspable handle is present; recessed grips and push-button-only models need no handle role
only when a distinct push control releases the door
only when controls form a distinct renderable panel or link
only when a display is separately segmented
only on models with a distinct rotating cooking platter
only when an over-range or ventilating microwave visibly segments this component

exclusive_or_alternative_role_groups.rule: A model may use a handle, a release button, an integrated grip, or powered opening; do not require either optional role.
Turntable and flat-floor configurations are alternatives; fixed_cavity_floor is contextual and never requires a separate link.

instance_discriminability_rules: The single main door needs no qualifier.
Repeated control buttons should use function labels when knowable; otherwise stable one-based ordinals are acceptable.
Multiple trays or racks, when present, use upper/lower or stable ordinal qualifiers.

minimal_required_roles.definition: the main appliance enclosure or tub-supporting body
the main closure providing access to the washing compartment
a load-bearing rack or basket that holds items during washing

optional_roles.presence_condition: only on models with a distinct third loading level
only when a distinct removable utensil basket is represented
only when a spray arm is externally visible and separately rendered
only when separately segmented on the door or tub
only when controls form a distinct renderable panel or link
only when a distinct handle is visible; pocket and integrated pulls need no separate role

exclusive_or_alternative_role_groups.rule: Two-rack and three-rack layouts are both valid; third_rack is never universally required.
A model may use either or both; score only visibly present distinct components.

instance_discriminability_rules: Two main racks should be identified as upper/lower or top/bottom rather than opaque rack numbers.
A third top loading level should be named third_rack, cutlery_rack, or another truthful specialization.
Repeated spray arms should use upper/lower/top/bottom qualifiers according to location.
Repeated rack wheels or tines may use a plural group name when fused into one renderable link; otherwise apply side and ordinal qualifiers.

oven.category_definition: standalone or built-in oven, excluding toaster ovens and microwave ovens

minimal_required_roles.definition: the main structural enclosure around the oven cavity
the closure providing access to an oven cavity
a support rack for cookware inside the oven cavity

optional_roles.presence_condition: only when controls form a distinct renderable panel or link
only on models with distinct rotary controls
only when separately segmented from the door
only for a convection model with a visible, separately rendered fan or fan assembly
only when a heating element is visibly modeled as a separate renderable link
only for a range or stove configuration; built-in wall ovens need no cooktop
only when a distinct lower drawer is present

exclusive_or_alternative_role_groups.rule: A cooktop and lower drawer may accompany a range oven but are not required for a built-in or wall oven.
Convection hardware is model-dependent; conventional_cavity is contextual and never requires a separate link.
Touch controls, buttons, and knobs may occur separately or together.

instance_discriminability_rules: In a double oven, doors and cavity-specific parts should use upper/lower or top/bottom qualifiers.
Multiple racks should use vertical-position qualifiers when stable; otherwise use one-based ordinals in bottom-to-top order.
Multiple heating elements should use functional or positional names such as bake_element and broil_element.
Repeated cooktop burners or knobs should use position and, when knowable, controlled-burner identity before ordinals.

faucet.category_definition: water-control faucet; tap is an accepted category synonym

minimal_required_roles.definition: the main mounted body or base carrying the faucet assembly
the outlet-bearing member that directs water into the basin or sink

optional_roles.presence_condition: only on manually controlled or touch-assisted models with a distinct handle
only when a rotary knob rather than a lever is distinctly modeled
only when a dedicated proximity or touch sensor is separately visible; a whole-body sensor needs no extra sensor link
only for a detachable pull-down or pull-out outlet head
only when a separate side-mounted sprayer is present
only when an exposed or separately rendered hose is present
only when the outlet aerator is visibly and separately segmented

exclusive_or_alternative_role_groups.rule: Manual lever/knob and hands-free sensing are alternative primary modes, but touch-assisted products may combine a handle with sensing; whole_body_sensor is contextual and requires no separate link.
Single-handle and two-handle layouts are both valid; do not require two handles universally.
Neither spray configuration is universal, and either is judged only when visibly present.

instance_discriminability_rules: A two-handle faucet should use hot/cold qualifiers when function is knowable; left/right is acceptable when only placement is supportable.
A single mixing handle needs no qualifier.
Distinguish the main spout from a side_sprayer or pull_out_spray_head when both are separate links.
Repeated valves or mounting elements use function, side, then stable ordinals in that priority order.

refrigerator.category_definition: refrigerator appliance; fridge and the release typo refrigerater are accepted category lexical variants

minimal_required_roles.definition: a hinged closure providing access to the refrigerated food compartment

optional_roles.presence_condition: only when the appliance includes a freezer compartment with a hinged closure
only when the freezer compartment is accessed by a sliding drawer
only when a shelf is a distinct renderable link
only when a distinct internal storage drawer is present
only when a distinct door-mounted storage bin or shelf is present
only when separately segmented; recessed, pocket, and integrated pulls need no separate role
only on models with a visible dispenser assembly
only when separately and visibly represented

exclusive_or_alternative_role_groups.rule: Single-door and French-door refrigerated compartments are both valid.
A refrigerator may have no freezer; if it has one, hinged-door and drawer access are alternatives and model-specific.
External water or ice dispensing is not universal; no_external_dispenser is contextual and requires no link.

instance_discriminability_rules: French-door pairs must distinguish left and right refrigerated doors.
Top-freezer and bottom-freezer closures must be distinguished from refrigerated-compartment doors by compartment and position.
Repeated shelves should use compartment plus vertical position when stable; otherwise use one-based ordinals in bottom-to-top order.
Repeated interior drawers should use function such as crisper or deli when knowable, then level or side, then stable ordinals.
Door handles should inherit the corresponding door's compartment and laterality when more than one handle is present.

limitations: This is a role-and-synonym gold, not an inventory of parts that every instance must contain.
Optional-role absence must never be interpreted as a method failure or missing semantic coverage.
Manufacturer terminology varies by region and model; listed synonyms are intentionally conservative rather than exhaustive.
The gold does not prescribe link granularity. A component fused into a larger renderable link need not appear as its own link.
Names alone cannot prove geometry, articulation axis, joint limits, physical validity, or actual appliance function.
A truthful unlisted term requires blind adjudication and must not be silently added after results are observed.
The role set covers externally visible and commonly modeled parts; hidden service components are outside scope unless visibly represented as distinct renderable geometry.
Source webpages may change after the frozen access time; their URLs and the access timestamp are provenance, not content-addressed snapshots.
No claim is made that benchmark assets contain any optional component described by the public sources.
The parent protocol's three-blind-judge gate and all other completeness gates remain in force.
